text.p: Portuguese cash bonds and futures slipped in late trade but dealers said 10-year bonds would continue to consolidate at recent record highs and three-year maturities had plenty of room to move higher.
Dealers said expectations that Portugal's year-on-year inflation rate for June might drop below two percent, reviving hopes of a cut in Bank of Portugal rates, would keep shorter bonds buoyant.
Analysts polled by Reuters forecast a year-on-year rate of between 2.0 percent and 2.4 percent. The inflation figure is due by Monday.

"Some domestic funds and foreign investors have been buying heavily at the short end and the interest is still there," said one trader. "If inflation turns out below two percent then the question isn't whether the Bank of Portugal will cut rates but whether it takes off 25 basis points or 50."
The escudo ended little changed at 100.91/94 per mark after opening at 100.95/101.00. Dealers said it would continue to trade in a range between 100.80 and 101.00 as long as the dollar stayed firm.
